content:
The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

$ taproot get component.avatar
# Avatar

Use Avatar to show a small picture of a person, so people can recognize who did, owns, or wrote something.

Shows a person as a small round picture. When there is no picture, or it fails to load, it shows the person's initials, and when there is no name either, a generic person symbol. It is not a control.

## When to use

- Show who wrote a comment or message, beside their name.
- Identify the signed-in person in an account area or settings header.
- Show who owns or is assigned to an item in a list or a card.

## When not to use

- Open a profile or account menu by pressing the avatar. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Avatar is not a control. Place it inside a Button or a Link, which give the action its role, focus, and accessible name.
- Show a symbol for a thing that is not a person, such as a file type or an app. Use [Icon](component.icon) instead. Icon sizes and colors a symbol at text scale. Avatar's fallback to initials only makes sense for a name.
- Show a photo or illustration as content, such as a product image or a cover. Instead: An image in the surrounding page. Avatar crops to a small circle, which suits a face, not content imagery.
- Show whether a person is online, busy, or away. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Avatar has no presence state in this version. Place a Badge, or text, beside it that states the status.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | container | The round area that crops its content and sets the avatar's size. |
| image | container | The supplied picture of the person, cropped to fill the surface. |
| initials | label | Up to two letters from the person's name, shown when there is no picture. |
| placeholder | indicator | A generic person symbol, shown when there is neither a picture nor a name. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | string |  |  | The person's full name. It is the avatar's accessible name, and its initials show when there is no picture. |
| image | string |  |  | Where the picture of the person is loaded from. Without it, or when it fails to load, the initials show instead. |
| size | enum | `small`, `medium`, `large` | `medium` |  |
| decorative | boolean |  | `false` | Hides the avatar from assistive technology. Use it when the person's name is shown beside the avatar. |

`size` values:

- `small`: Fixed small size, for dense lists and beside small text.
- `medium`: Fixed medium size, beside body text, such as the author of a comment.
- `large`: Fixed large size, for a profile or account header.

## States

`default`

## Rules

### Content

- **SHOULD** picture-shows-face: Use a square picture centered on the person's face, so the circular crop keeps the face whole.

### Behavior

- **MUST** fallback-order: The avatar shows the picture when it loads. When there is no picture, or it fails to load, it shows the initials. When there is no name either, it shows the placeholder symbol. It shows exactly one of the three.
- **MUST** initials-from-name: The initials are the first letter of the name's first word and the first letter of its last word, in uppercase. A one-word name gives one letter.
  - Do: Ada Lovelace shows AL; Grace Brewster Murray Hopper shows GH; Prince shows P
- **MUST** not-a-control: The avatar is not focusable and does not activate.
- **MUST** fixed-circle: The avatar occupies a circle of its size whether or not the picture has loaded, so the layout does not shift. The picture fills the circle and is cropped, never stretched.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** named-by-person: An avatar with a name that is not decorative is exposed to assistive technology as an image named with the person's name. An avatar that is decorative, or has no name, is hidden from assistive technology.
- **SHOULD** decorative-beside-name: Mark the avatar decorative when the person's name is shown beside it, so assistive technology does not read the name twice.
  - Do: A decorative avatar beside the author name of a comment
  - Avoid: A named avatar directly beside the same name in text
- **MUST** forced-colors: In forced-colors mode the circle has a visible edge, and the initials and placeholder stay visible.

## Accessibility

- Role: Image when named. Otherwise hidden from assistive technology.
- Name: From the name parameter. None when decorative or when there is no name.

## Rationale

- **Sizes are named small, medium, and large, like Icon and Spinner.** The system has two size vocabularies: Button uses sm and md, while Icon and Spinner use small, medium, and large. Avatar follows the larger and more recent group until the naming is settled for every component. There is no inherit size, because an avatar is a picture with its own size, not a symbol that matches the text around it.
- **Sizes use spacing primitives and the large initials use a text primitive.** No semantic size role exists (token

# Badge

Use Badge for status or metadata. It is not a control.

Labels status or metadata. Not a control.

## When to use

- Display status, category, or supporting metadata.

## When not to use

- Trigger an action in the current view. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
- Navigate to another location. Use [Link](component.link) instead. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.
- Announce a live status change by itself. Use [Alert](component.alert) instead. Badge sets no live-region role. Alert announces its message when asked to.
- Explain a status in a sentence or offer an action that resolves it. Use [Alert](component.alert) instead. Badge is a short label. Alert holds a message and actions.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | indicator | Non-interactive label surface. |
| content | label | Short status or metadata text, with an optional leading icon. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | enum | `default`, `accent`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info` | `default` |  |

`variant` values:

- `default`: Neutral metadata or categorization. Example: Default
- `accent`: Brand emphasis without implying status. Example: Accent
- `success`: Successful or active state. Example: Active
- `danger`: Failed or blocked status, not a destructive action. Example: Failed
- `warning`: Condition that needs attention. Example: Pending
- `info`: Informational state or feature label. Example: Beta

## States

`default`

## Rules

### Content

- **SHOULD** keep-label-short: Keep the label short.

### Behavior

- **MUST** not-a-control: Badge is not a control. It is not focusable and does not activate.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** text-communicates-state: The text communicates the state. Meaning does not depend on color alone.
- **MUST** no-live-region: Badge does not set a live-region role. The surrounding UI announces a status change that must be announced.

## Accessibility

- Role: Non-interactive text
- Name: Visible text is the accessible name.

## Rationale

- **Badge consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. No component-token namespace.
- **The gap between a leading icon and the label uses a spacing primitive.** Tokens ADR 0003 allows a primitive when no semantic role exists, as for padding. Badge is denser than Button, so it uses the smaller step.
- **Badge is non-interactive and sets no live-region role.** Status that must be announced belongs to the surrounding UI.

- [Alert](component.alert) — Explain a status in a sentence or offer an action that resolves it. Badge is a short label. Alert holds a message and actions.
- [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action in the current view. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
- [Link](component.link) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.

### alternative-to

- [Alert](component.alert) — Label a status or category on an item in a list or table. Badge is a compact label on an item. Alert is a message in the flow of the page.
- [Avatar](component.avatar) — Show whether a person is online, busy, or away. Avatar has no presence state in this version. Place a Badge, or text, beside it that states the status.
- [Button](component.button) — Display status or metadata. Button communicates an available action.
- [Card](component.card) — Label a status or category on an item. Badge is a compact label. Place a Badge inside a card when the card's subject has a status.
- [Link](component.link) — Display status or metadata. Link communicates a destination.

# Compose or propose

Compose a new interface need from tokens and existing components first, and open an issue or RFC only when the system itself has to change.

Most interface needs are met by composing what the system already publishes. Change the system
only when composition cannot express the need without copying or overriding a component.

## Compose first

Work through these in order and stop at the first one that meets the need:

1. A published variant, size, or parameter of an existing component.
2. Existing components placed together in product markup, such as a Badge beside a Button or a
   Link after an action group.
3. Product layout and chrome styled with semantic tokens. Use a primitive token only when no
   semantic role expresses the choice.

A composition that meets the need stays in product code. It does not need an issue, a record, or
a review.

## Do not fork a component

Composition stops being composition when product code rebuilds what a component owns. Do not:

- Copy a component's styles or structure to make a variant that the contract does not publish.
- Restyle a component's internal parts, or override the tokens it reads, to create a variant,
  state, or size the contract does not publish.
- Define component tokens in product code.
- Use one component to do another's job, such as a Badge as a control or a Link styled as a
  Button. The action hierarchy pattern says which control fits which job.
- Rebuild a component's states, focus ring, or accessible name handling in a new element.

When one of these is the only way to meet the need, the system is missing something. Propose it.

## Propose a change

Open an issue on the design system when the change fits the components and tokens it already has:

- A variant, size, or parameter on an existing component.
- A bug in a component, one of its implementations, a token, or its documentation.
- A composition used in more than one place that should become a pattern.
- A new component whose behavior comes from a standard platform control plus tokens, such as an
  icon or a field shell.

Some changes alter how the system works, not only what it contains. Say so in the issue, so the
design question is settled before anyone writes code:

- A component that owns focus management, an overlay, or a composite keyboard model, such as a
  Dialog, Select, Menu, or Tabs.
- A new token tier, or a semantic role category that does not exist yet.

Use **Avatar** for the picture and **Badge** for the online status, placed side by side. Avatar has no presence state of its own, and its record points to Badge or plain text for this (`component.avatar`, "When not to use").

| Need | Component | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Picture | Avatar | Set `name` and `image`, plus a `size` of `small`, `medium` or `large`. If the picture is missing or fails to load, it falls back to initials. |
| Online | Badge | Use `variant="success"` (successful or active state) with the text "Online". |
| Offline | Badge | Use `variant="default"` with the text "Offline". |

- **Status text (MUST):** the Badge must say the status in words, because meaning can't depend on color alone (`component.badge#text-communicates-state`). This rules out a bare green dot.
- **Dot on the avatar:** Avatar doesn't offer an overlaid presence dot, and restyling its internals to add one would count as forking the component under `guideline.compose-or-propose`. If you want that look, propose it to the design system as a new parameter.
- **Name beside the avatar (SHOULD):** if the person's name is shown next to it, set `decorative` so screen readers don't read the name twice (`component.avatar#decorative-beside-name`).
- **Live updates (MUST):** Badge doesn't announce changes itself (`component.badge#no-live-region`). If a status change needs announcing, the surrounding UI has to do it, for example with Alert, though most presence changes probably don't need it.
- **Clickable avatars (MUST):** Avatar isn't a control (`component.avatar#not-a-control`). To make it open a profile, put it inside a Button or Link.

Before writing code, run `node_modules/.bin/taproot get component.avatar --impl web` to get the exact import and attribute names, and do the same for `component.badge`. Avatar's record only lists a web implementation in the search results, while Badge has both web and React.
